from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # === Data and Setup ===
        title = "The Search Dilemma: Classical vs. Quantum"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Finding one item in N takes N/2 classical tries.",
            "For 1,000 items, that's about 500 attempts.",
            "Quantum search needs only about 32 tries.",
            "This speedup is known as Grover's Algorithm.",
            "It scales with the square root of N."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Mobject Preparation ===
        # Grid of 100 white squares representing N items
        grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2) for _ in range(100)])
        grid.arrange_in_grid(10, 10, buff=0.05)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # Labels and Formulas
        classical_label = Text("Classical Search: O(N)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(classical_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        quantum_label = Text("Quantum Search: O(√N)", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_label, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        formula = Text("√1000 ≈ 32", font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Scan line for quantum processing
        scan_line = Line(
            grid.get_top() + UP*0.2, 
            grid.get_bottom() + DOWN*0.2, 
            color="#00FFFF", 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        scan_line.set_x(grid.get_left()[0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Finding one item in N takes N/2 classical tries."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(
            Create(grid),
            FadeIn(classical_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "For 1,000 items, that's about 500 attempts."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        # Sequentially highlight 50 squares in red
        highlight_anims = [
            grid[i].animate.set_fill("#FF0000", opacity=0.8).set_color("#FF0000") 
            for i in range(50)
        ]
        self.play(LaggedStart(*highlight_anims, lag_ratio=0.04, run_time=3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Quantum search needs only about 32 tries."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Clear red highlights and switch labels
        self.play(
            FadeOut(classical_label),
            FadeIn(quantum_label),
            *[grid[i].animate.set_fill(opacity=0).set_color(WHITE) for i in range(50)],
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "This speedup is known as Grover's Algorithm."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Fast cyan scan line passing across the grid
        self.add(scan_line)
        self.play(
            scan_line.animate.set_x(grid.get_right()[0]), 
            run_time=1.5, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(scan_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "It scales with the square root of N."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Highlight target square in green and show formula
        target_idx = 42
        self.play(
            grid[target_idx].animate.set_fill("#00FF00", opacity=1.0).set_color("#00FF00"),
            Write(formula),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Superposition and State Representation", [
            "Quantum computers search all possibilities simultaneously.",
            "We start by putting all states into superposition.",
            "Every state now has the same probability amplitude."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a bar graph with 8 white (#FFFFFF) vertical bars of equal height, labeled |000> through |111> at the base.
        
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=2.0, width=0.3, fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=1, color="#FFFFFF")
            for _ in range(8)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        
        labels = VGroup(*[
            Text(f"|{bin(i)[2:].zfill(3)}>", font_size=14, color="#FFFFFF")
            for i in range(8)
        ])
        
        for i in range(8):
            labels[i].next_to(bars[i], DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
        graph_group = VGroup(bars, labels)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(bars), Write(labels), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Apply a cyan glow (#00FFFF) to all 8 bars simultaneously to represent the state of 'superposition'.
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            *[bar.animate.set_fill("#00FFFF").set_stroke("#00FFFF", width=2) for bar in bars],
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the text 'Equal Probability' in light grey (#AAAAAA) above the bars as they pulse.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        prob_text = Text("Equal Probability", font_size=24, color="#AAAAAA")
        # Center in the "A" row
        self.place_in_area(prob_text, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prob_text, shift=UP))
        
        # Pulsing effect for bars and text
        # Using a loop for pulse
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                bars.animate.scale(1.1),
                prob_text.animate.scale(1.1),
                rate_func=there_and_back,
                run_time=1.0
            )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the lecture content
        title = "Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)"
        lines = [
            "The Oracle function marks the correct answer.",
            "It flips the target state's amplitude to negative.",
            "Other amplitudes remain positive and unchanged.",
            "The target is now mathematically distinct from others.",
            "This phase inversion prepares for the next step."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_TARGET = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_OTHER = "#FFFFFF"   # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Oracle function marks the correct answer.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_TARGET)
        
        # Create 8 bars representing the amplitudes of 3 qubits
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(
                width=0.3, 
                height=1.5, 
                fill_opacity=1, 
                fill_color=COLOR_OTHER, 
                stroke_width=1, 
                stroke_color=COLOR_OTHER
            ) for _ in range(8)
        ])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        # Highlight the 6th bar (index 5) for state |101>
        bars[5].set_fill(COLOR_TARGET)
        bars[5].set_stroke(COLOR_TARGET)
        
        # Labels for the states - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        labels = VGroup(*[
            Text(f"|{i:03b}⟩", font_size=18, color=WHITE) 
            for i in range(8)
        ])
        for i, label in enumerate(labels):
            label.next_to(bars[i], DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
        chart = VGroup(bars, labels)
        # Position the chart in the grid area
        self.place_in_area(chart, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Oracle target icon
        target_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_TARGET, stroke_width=2),
            Line(LEFT*0.2, RIGHT*0.2, color=COLOR_TARGET, stroke_width=2),
            Line(UP*0.2, DOWN*0.2, color=COLOR_TARGET, stroke_width=2)
        ).next_to(bars[5], UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(chart))
        self.play(Create(target_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It flips the target state's amplitude to negative.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_TARGET)
        
        # Perform the phase inversion (flip the bar across the x-axis)
        self.play(
            Rotate(
                bars[5], 
                angle=PI, 
                axis=RIGHT, 
                about_point=bars[5].get_bottom()
            ),
            labels[5].animate.shift(DOWN * 1.5), # Shift label down to stay below the flipped bar
            FadeOut(target_icon, shift=DOWN), # The icon has done its job
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Other amplitudes remain positive and unchanged.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_OTHER)
        
        # Highlight the unchanged bars
        other_bars = VGroup(*[bars[i] for i in range(8) if i != 5])
        self.play(
            other_bars.animate.set_opacity(0.5),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            other_bars.animate.set_opacity(1.0),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The target is now mathematically distinct from others.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_TARGET)
        
        # Add negative sign next to the inverted bar
        neg_sign = Text("-", color=COLOR_TARGET, font_size=36)
        neg_sign.next_to(bars[5], LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(neg_sign))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This phase inversion prepares for the next step.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_OTHER)
        
        # Final highlight of the result
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(bars[5], neg_sign), color=COLOR_TARGET))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculate the average height of all amplitudes.",
            "Reflect every amplitude across this average line.",
            "The negative target amplitude shoots up high.",
            "Wrong answers shrink closer to zero height.",
            "This is the power of amplitude amplification."
        ]
        
        # Colors
        ORANGE = "#FF8C00"
        YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Setup
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Positioning logic
        baseline_y = self.grid["D1"][1]
        h = 0.8  # Reference height unit
        
        def create_bar(index, height, color):
            # Create a rectangle with the base at baseline_y
            rect = Rectangle(
                width=0.4, 
                height=abs(height), 
                fill_opacity=0.8, 
                color=color, 
                stroke_width=2,
                fill_color=color
            )
            x_pos = 0.8 + index * 0.6
            # Position the bar so it grows from the baseline
            if height >= 0:
                rect.move_to([x_pos, baseline_y + abs(height)/2, 0])
            else:
                rect.move_to([x_pos, baseline_y - abs(height)/2, 0])
            return rect

        # Initial state: 7 white bars at +h, 1 yellow bar at -h (index 4)
        bars = VGroup(*[
            create_bar(i, h if i != 4 else -h, WHITE_COLOR if i != 4 else YELLOW)
            for i in range(8)
        ])
        
        self.add(bars)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Calculate the average height of all amplitudes."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        
        # Average height = (7*h - h)/8 = 0.75*h
        avg_h = 0.75 * h
        avg_y = baseline_y + avg_h
        
        avg_line = DashedLine(
            start=[0.5, avg_y, 0],
            end=[5.5, avg_y, 0],
            color=ORANGE
        )
        avg_label = Text("Average", font_size=16, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(avg_label, "C6")
        avg_label.next_to(avg_line, UP, buff=0.1).set_x(5.0)

        self.play(Create(avg_line), Write(avg_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Reflect every amplitude across this average line."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        
        # Reflect logic: y_new = 2*y_avg - y_old
        # Normal bars: 2*0.75h - h = 0.5h
        # Target bar: 2*0.75h - (-h) = 2.5h
        reflected_bars = VGroup(*[
            create_bar(i, 0.5 * h if i != 4 else 2.5 * h, WHITE_COLOR if i != 4 else YELLOW)
            for i in range(8)
        ])

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(bars, reflected_bars),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The negative target amplitude shoots up high."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        target_bar = reflected_bars[4]
        # Emphasis on growth
        self.play(
            target_bar.animate.set_fill(opacity=1.0).scale(1.1, about_edge=DOWN),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(target_bar.animate.scale(1/1.1, about_edge=DOWN), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Wrong answers shrink closer to zero height."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        other_bars = VGroup(*[reflected_bars[i] for i in range(8) if i != 4])
        self.play(
            other_bars.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This is the power of amplitude amplification."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        
        # Highlight success with a flash
        flash_point = target_bar.get_top()
        flash = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).move_to(flash_point)
        self.play(
            flash.animate.scale(15).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1,
            rate_func=exponential_decay
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching latest lecture lines from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "Repeat these steps approximately square root N times.",
            "The target amplitude becomes nearly 100 percent.",
            "Measuring the system reveals the needle immediately."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Iteration and Measurement", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors based on storyboard and constraints
        COLOR_REPEAT = "#AAAAAA"
        COLOR_TARGET = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_MEASURE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SUCCESS = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_DEFAULT = "#444444"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Repeat icon (circular 'repeat' icon in light grey #AAAAAA)
        repeat_icon = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=1.5*PI, color=COLOR_REPEAT)
        repeat_icon.add_tip()
        self.place_at_grid(repeat_icon, "A5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Bars setup (8 bars)
        bars = VGroup()
        target_index = 4 # Representing Safe #5 (index 4)
        num_bars = 8
        bar_width = 0.3
        
        for i in range(num_bars):
            h = 0.4 if i != target_index else 0.8
            c = COLOR_DEFAULT if i != target_index else COLOR_TARGET
            bar = Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=h, fill_opacity=0.8, color=c, fill_color=c)
            bars.add(bar)
        
        # Arrange bars in area D1 to E6
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "D1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Initial reveal and lecture color change
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_REPEAT))
        self.play(Create(repeat_icon), Create(bars))
        
        # Yellow target bar pulses and grows taller while repeat icon rotates
        target_bar = bars[target_index]
        self.play(
            Rotate(repeat_icon, angle=-2*PI, about_point=repeat_icon.get_center()),
            target_bar.animate.scale(1.3, about_edge=DOWN),
            run_time=2, rate_func=there_and_back
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_TARGET))
        
        # Target bar reaching near-maximum height while all other bars shrink to nearly zero.
        target_final_height = 2.5
        others_final_height = 0.05
        
        anim_group = []
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            new_h = target_final_height if i == target_index else others_final_height
            anim_group.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_h, about_edge=DOWN))
        
        self.play(
            *anim_group,
            FadeOut(repeat_icon),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_SUCCESS))
        
        # Measurement meter icon (#FFFFFF)
        meter_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=COLOR_MEASURE)
        meter_line = Line(meter_arc.get_left(), meter_arc.get_right(), color=COLOR_MEASURE)
        meter_needle = Line(meter_arc.get_center(), meter_arc.get_center() + UP * 0.45, color=COLOR_MEASURE)
        meter = VGroup(meter_arc, meter_line, meter_needle)
        self.place_at_grid(meter, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(meter))
        
        # Needle "measuring" animation
        self.play(Rotate(meter_needle, angle=-PI/4, about_point=meter_arc.get_center()), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(Rotate(meter_needle, angle=PI/2, about_point=meter_arc.get_center()), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(Rotate(meter_needle, angle=-PI/4, about_point=meter_arc.get_center()), run_time=0.3)
        
        # All bars vanish except target which turns solid green (#00FF00)
        vanish_anims = [FadeOut(bars[i]) for i in range(num_bars) if i != target_index]
        
        self.play(
            *vanish_anims,
            target_bar.animate.set_color(COLOR_SUCCESS).set_fill(COLOR_SUCCESS),
            FadeOut(meter),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Grover's Algorithm: The Quantum Needle in a Haystack
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science students and tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Search Dilemma: Classical vs. Quantum
sections.content: Introduce the concept of searching an unstructured database. Explain that classically, finding 1 specific item among N items takes N/2 tries on average (O(N)). In the quantum world, we can do it in roughly √N steps.
sections.example: Imagine a wall of 1,000 identical locked safes. Alice has one key that fits only one safe. Classically, she might have to try 500+ safes. With Grover's Algorithm, she only needs about 32 'quantum tries'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Superposition and State Representation
sections.content: Briefly explain that a quantum computer doesn't look at one safe at a time. We put all possible states into a 'superposition', represented visually as a bar graph where every state has the same positive amplitude (height).
sections.example: Visualizing 8 safes (3 qubits) as 8 equal-height vertical bars on a graph. This is our starting line: every possibility is equally likely.

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Oracle'—a function that recognizes the correct answer. It doesn't tell us where the answer is; it simply 'marks' it. Mathematically, it flips the sign of the target state's amplitude from positive to negative.
sections.example: In our bar graph of 8 bars, the Oracle identifies Safe #5. The bar for #5 flips upside down (below the X-axis), while the other 7 bars remain unchanged. It's now 'mathematically distinct' but not yet 'measurable'.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
sections.content: Explain the 'Grover Diffusion Operator'. We calculate the average height of all bars. Then, we reflect every bar across this average line. Because the target bar was negative, this reflection makes it shoot up much higher than the others, while the others shrink.
sections.example: Graphically: Draw a dotted horizontal line representing the 'Average Height'. Flip all bars across this line. Safe #5 (the negative one) undergoes a massive growth spurt, while the wrong safes drop closer to zero. This is 'Amplitude Amplification'.

sections.title: Iteration and Measurement
sections.content: Explain that we repeat Steps 1 and 2 approximately √N times. Each iteration makes the 'right' answer's amplitude taller and the 'wrong' ones shorter. Finally, we measure the system, and it collapses into the correct state with near-certainty.
sections.example: After 2 or 3 iterations for our 8-safe example, the bar for Safe #5 is nearly 100% of the total height. When Alice 'opens' the quantum safe, she finds the prize immediately. The Cheetah (Quantum) has finished while the Turtle (Classical) is still at the first few safes.

storyboard.title: The Search Dilemma: Classical vs. Quantum
lecture_lines: Finding one item in N takes N/2 classical tries.
For 1,000 items, that's about 500 attempts.
Quantum search needs only about 32 tries.
This speedup is known as Grover's Algorithm.
It scales with the square root of N.

lecture_lines: Quantum computers search all possibilities simultaneously.
We start by putting all states into superposition.
Every state now has the same probability amplitude.

Apply a cyan glow (#00FFFF) to all 8 bars simultaneously to represent the state of 'superposition'.

storyboard.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: The Oracle function marks the correct answer.
It flips the target state's amplitude to negative.
Other amplitudes remain positive and unchanged.
The target is now mathematically distinct from others.
This phase inversion prepares for the next step.
animations: Start with 8 equal white (#FFFFFF) bars; highlight the 6th bar (labeled |101>) in yellow (#FFFF00).
Draw the target icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] above the yellow bar to represent the Oracle's identification.

Keep the other 7 bars stationary and white (#FFFFFF) while the target bar stays yellow and inverted.
Fade in a negative sign '-' in yellow (#FFFF00) next to the inverted bar.

storyboard.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Calculate the average height of all amplitudes.
Reflect every amplitude across this average line.
The negative target amplitude shoots up high.
Wrong answers shrink closer to zero height.
This is the power of amplitude amplification.
animations: Draw a horizontal dashed line in orange (#FF8C00) across the graph representing the average height of all bars.
Animate each bar moving to its reflected position across the orange dashed line.
The inverted yellow bar (#FFFF00) shoots upward, becoming significantly taller than its original positive height.
The 7 white bars (#FFFFFF) move downward, shrinking to a much smaller height near the X-axis.
Highlight the target bar's peak with a white flash (#FFFFFF) to emphasize 'Amplitude Amplification'.

storyboard.title: Iteration and Measurement
lecture_lines: Repeat these steps approximately square root N times.
The target amplitude becomes nearly 100 percent.
Measuring the system reveals the needle immediately.
animations: Show a circular 'repeat' icon in light grey (#AAAAAA) while the yellow target bar (#FFFF00) pulses and grows taller.
Animate the target bar (#FFFF00) reaching near-maximum height while all other bars shrink to nearly zero.
A measurement meter icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/meter.svg] appears; all bars vanish except the target bar which turns solid green (#00FF00).
